newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power weaker amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power weaker amid mild weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. Monday were weaker than Friday's levels following a weekend moderation from a bout of frigid temperatures in the region.
"It stayed soft today," a Southeast trader said.

For Tuesday, temperatures in the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) district were forecast to peak in 50s-70s Fahrenheit and to bottom in 20s-50s. Those in Florida were predicted to peak in 70s-80s and to bottom in 50s-60s.
Reduced output this past weekend at Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) Sequoyah 1 nuclear power unit did not have noticeable effect on today's trading, market sources said.
Some sources noted TVA planned the cutback for scheduled maintenance, and had sufficient power supply to meet native load ahead of the outage.
The 1,148 megawatt (MW) unit in Soddy-Daisy, Tenn., was expected to resume full output shortly. those sources said. TVA, as a matter of policy, does not comment on the status of its nuclear operation
Peak, firm electricity for Tuesday delivery into northwestern part of TVA territory was assessed at $17.00-$18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Friday's trades near $19.50 for Monday.
Firm deliveries during light-load hours on Tuesday was pegged at $13.00-$15.00, a wider range than $13.00-$15.00 on Friday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, next-day electricity for firm, peak delivery was notationally valued at $21.00-$23.00, sharply lower than Friday's quote of $25.75-$26.00.
Firm, off-peak Ga./Fla. power deliveries for Tuesday were assessed at $17.00-$18.00, compared with a quote of $18.00 on Friday for Monday.
In the Florida pennisula, 12-hour block power scheduled among the state's utilities for Tuesday was heard offered $23.00-$25.50, compared with Friday's $24.00-$25.00.
Most marketers anticipated a return of cold weather later this week to the Southeast would bolster spot power prices.
Entergy Corp's 858 MW Arkansas 2 nuclear unit was shut Saturday, and was expected to remain shut for about three weeks.
Market sources said wholesale power trading was light due to participants attending an industry conference in New Orlean for the next couple of days.
